query: Fire in the Workshop The workshop is on fire. Properly this time. Mir is in the doorway, coughing — and trying to go back in. "My notebooks! Three years of notes!" Grab the notebooks You come out singed, smoking, with an armful of notebooks. Mir stares at you, then at the notebooks, then bursts into tears and hugs you, both of you coughing. You get halfway before the smoke drives you back. You save one notebook. Mir says it's the most important one. You both know it isn't. They mean it anyway. Drag Mir away You haul Mir back from the door. The notebooks burn. Mir is silent for a week. Then they start a new notebook. The first page just says: "Thank you." The next morning you find them soldering on the corridor floor outside the burnt door, and bring them a cushion, and tea. Freeze the fire out You throw frost at the doorway until the flames grey over and give up with a hiss. The notebooks are wet, cold and whole. Mir hugs them, then you, then the notebooks again, shivering.

The Notebooks
Mir holds out a notebook, one of a stack, battered and bristling with slips of paper. "Three years," they say. "Every idea. Some of them work. Probably. Nobody's read them. You can, if you want. Carefully. Very carefully. With clean hands."
